method: Treated each invariant as a universal proposition and separately asked whether its falsifiedBy sentence logically falsifies that proposition.
Built an interaction matrix across TO pairs and EC pairs instead of assessing each sentence in isolation. This found contradictions that a per-row source crosswalk misses.
Kept process termination class, policy verdict, reason/error diagnostics, evidence authority, and attempt identity as separate types while reviewing wording.
Grounded disputed interactions against architecture/02, /03, /05, /07, /08, versioning-policy.v1, and the retained D9 v1.5 semantic classes/invariants.
Did not treat RESTORED/NARROWED labels or author-provided falsifiers as evidence of correctness.
whatCouldHaveFailed: A locally plausible invariant could contradict a different invariant in the same set.
A correct safety principle could be stated with the wrong scope and prohibit valid advisory or recovery behavior.
An exit class could be confused with a precise user remedy even though reason codes deliberately refine it.
A whole-Run parity assertion could be impossible because attempt identity must differ.
Fail-closed wording could collapse verdict and termination after the set explicitly separates them.
A falsifier could reject a valid stronger implementation or merely restate the invariant's negation.

summary.overall: The set is not correct as a whole. Five propositions are correct as stated, five are sound only with scope edits, four are partly correct but require substantive rewrite, four are incorrect as stated, and TO-8 is an unsettled compatibility policy rather than an established invariant.

perInvariant.assessment: One total host termination algebra is the correct architecture. 'Every command kind' does not clearly include pre-admission failures, process-start failures, or the controlled stop of a long-lived server, and it does not exclude SIGKILL/runtime death outside host control.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Every host-controlled termination of a finite invocation, including pre-admission and non-analysis commands, resolves to exactly one named HostTermination class. Long-lived commands acquire a termination only when they stop; uncontrollable process death is explicitly outside the contract.

perInvariant.assessment: One logical policy owner and one boundary adapter per process invocation prevent split-brain exits. 'Exactly one write site' globally is too source-shape-specific when the product may have multiple process entrypoints; two sites in different binaries are not automatically a violation.
perInvariant.requiredWording: For each process entrypoint, one host finalizer owns termination derivation and one boundary adapter applies it on every controllable path.

perInvariant.assessment: Lower layers must not choose a numeric code or final class. Their typed domain results necessarily influence host interpretation, so 'maps to an exit' must not be read as forbidding typed failure categories or external-tool status translation inside an adapter.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Producers, rules, providers, and typed faults never select or carry a process exit/class; they return typed domain evidence for the host finalizer to interpret.

perInvariant.assessment: Verdict and termination answer different questions. A verdict may be absent before Run admission, or may remain pass while termination is operational-failed; every applicable projection must preserve that distinction.
perInvariant.requiredWording: No substantive change; add that verdict is optional where no policy evaluation occurred.

perInvariant.assessment: This combines three different rules and loses their qualifiers. 'Required partial coverage' is not a coherent condition: globally partial Coverage may still satisfy the predicate's required relations. A durability failure forbids termination success only when durability/authority was required; it does not erase a previously computed pass verdict. Export failure never changes the local verdict, although required delivery may change termination. 'Green outcome' collapses the axes TO-4 separated.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Split into: (a) unmet required Coverage makes the authoritative verdict indeterminate, never pass; (b) failure of a required authoritative durability postcondition makes termination non-success while preserving any computed verdict as a distinct field; (c) export/delivery never changes the local verdict, while required delivery may make termination operational-failed.

perInvariant.assessment: Finalization needs a linearization point and post-commit signals cannot reclassify it. The current falsifier's two runs may differ because one signal arrived before finalization, which is allowed; 'identical' also hides the event history.
perInvariant.requiredWording: A signal observed after the finalization commit cannot alter the committed termination. Falsifier: inject the same signal immediately after the recorded commit and observe any class/code change.

perInvariant.assessment: The architecture deliberately places distinct remedies behind one coarse exit class. Exit 3 covers convergence exhaustion (retry) and missing required capability (widen scope/install provider); sealed diagnostics require separate reason codes because the remedies differ. Exit 2 likewise groups usage, configuration, compatibility, identity, and mutation-precondition failures. Therefore 'two remedies behind one code is a defect' contradicts architecture/07.
perInvariant.requiredWording: An exit class is a stable automation/CI disposition. Reason/error codes distinguish precise operator remedies within that class. Different automation dispositions must not share a numeric code; diagnostics with different remedies must not share a reason code.

perInvariant.assessment: Never renumbering or repurposing an externally held code is sound. 'Additive-only, permanently' is stronger than established evidence, omits removal from its falsifier, and does not specify how old strict consumers handle a newly added class or how schema-family/major negotiation interacts with additions. VERSIONING remains CANDIDATE and currently points back to stale D9 v1.4, so ownership is not closed.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Within a contract family, an existing class/code meaning is never renumbered or repurposed. Removal, reservation, and addition behavior—including old-consumer handling—are owned by an explicitly one-way VERSIONING dependency.

perInvariant.assessment: Totality is correct only over a named primary automation partition. The text names no six classes and says a state requiring two remedies falsifies the model, although simultaneous faults can legitimately require several diagnostics/remedies. The finalizer needs deterministic primary-class precedence, not a claim that reality contains one remedy.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Every controlled terminal state selects exactly one primary class from success, policy-failed, request-rejected, indeterminate, operational-failed, interrupted under defined precedence. Multiple underlying diagnostics/remedies may coexist but cannot change that single primary automation disposition.

perInvariant.assessment: Unavailable evidence must not masquerade as a complete successful answer. Restricting the invariant to an empty payload misses false non-empty partial success; applying it absolutely would also forbid explicitly best-effort queries that return partial data with honest Coverage. Its falsifier is broader than the literal empty-only wording.
perInvariant.requiredWording: A result that claims to satisfy a required/authoritative query or evaluation cannot terminate success when required Coverage is insufficient, regardless of result cardinality. A separately typed best-effort projection may return partial data only with explicit Coverage and no complete-answer claim.

perInvariant.assessment: Fail-closed means no authoritative sealed success from corrupted required state; it does not mean a policy verdict field can never exist. A verdict may have been computed before a durability/publication fault and must remain distinct from operational termination under TO-4. An unrelated corrupt cache may also be quarantined and recomputed. The falsifier incorrectly treats pass/fail verdict and operational termination as alternatives.
perInvariant.requiredWording: An integrity fault affecting required inputs, evidence, ledger, or publication prevents authoritative sealing and forces operational-failed termination. Any already-computed verdict remains a distinct non-authoritative projection; unrelated corrupt acceleration state may be discarded and recomputed before proceeding.

perInvariant.assessment: Absence of a lifetime flag is local surface form, not semantic lifetime neutrality. Hidden module state, provider reuse, cancellation, cleanup, progress, or publication can vary by lifetime without a parameter/field/environment branch.
perInvariant.requiredWording: The declared execution boundary is re-entrant and lifetime-independent: under identical resolved Snapshot, Plan, toolchain, environment, grants, budgets, and exact Coverage, one-shot and resident execution produce identical EvidenceDigest/evaluation outcomes and equivalent cancellation, cleanup, and progress semantics. Performance and attempt identity are excluded.

perInvariant.assessment: Core semantic neutrality, whether a resident host ships, autostart/default policy, and project scope are separable decisions. The latter decisions are conditional on shipping residency and may impose requirements on the boundary without being entailed by EC-1.
perInvariant.requiredWording: No substantive change; state that autostart and scope decisions are conditional on choosing to ship residency.

perInvariant.assessment: Warm state must never become evidence authority. Comparing an identical whole Run is impossible alongside EC-6 because ExecutionId differs per attempt; clocks and lifecycle also differ. The governing comparison is EvidenceDigest, evaluation outcomes, and exact Coverage under fully equal semantic inputs.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Warm state may change only cost. Under identical Snapshot, Plan, toolchain, environment, grants, budgets, and exact Coverage, cold and resident executions yield identical EvidenceDigest and evaluation outcomes; attempt/lifecycle identities and timing are excluded.

perInvariant.assessment: Every supported evidence-writing topology must preserve multi-process storage integrity through a shared protocol. A deployment-specific mechanism or argument is not itself a violation: an enforced single-writer service or OS lock may implement the protocol correctly. Unsupported topologies may be rejected at admission.
perInvariant.requiredWording: The storage protocol states and enforces the concurrency preconditions for every supported evidence-writing topology; no host may assume absent concurrent writers unless admission enforces that assumption. Falsify with corruption, partial visibility, lost committed writes, or unenforced concurrency preconditions.

perInvariant.assessment: Integrity without guaranteed liveness for every contender is the right contract, and a typed bounded busy result is legitimate. A design promising both contenders complete does not violate it if transactions serialize and both actually complete.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Keep the proposition. Replace the falsifier with any corrupt/partial/lost publication, unbounded wait beyond declared policy, or contention failure that is not typed and distinguishable.

perInvariant.assessment: ExecutionId is allocated per admitted attempt, including retries and concurrent identical work; deterministic content identity belongs to Snapshot/Plan/FactView/EvidenceDigest. Allocation ownership should be assigned to host admission, outside the execution core.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Add host-admission ownership and collision/uniqueness expectations; retain the attempt/content distinction.

perInvariant.assessment: Direct core modules should not import ambient authority, and named adapters/providers must be honest TCB or actually OS-confined. Static import/call closure proves only absence within the declared static boundary; it cannot establish absence across dynamic loading, FFI/native code, injected implementations, or unexecuted runtime paths. Declared authority is not confinement.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Define the exact static/runtime core boundary. Static closure proves no direct ambient reach in covered modules; dynamic/native limits are disclosed. Named TCB adapters declare grants and are trusted, while untrusted adapters require an independently specified OS/runtime denial mechanism.

perInvariant.assessment: Admission, grants, contribution resolution, and process supervision correctly belong outside the core, but this is not yet an explicit four-way responsibility boundary. Provider execution, fact/rule/policy evaluation, budget accounting, storage reads/publication/finalization, cancellation, and telemetry are unassigned. The falsifier checks only three host responsibilities.
perInvariant.requiredWording: Provide a complete inside/outside ownership table for core, host, provider, and storage; place effectful provider execution, publication/finalization, cancellation, telemetry, budgets, and policy. Derive falsifiers from every boundary crossing.

interactionFindings.title: TO-7 contradicts the sealed diagnostic/remedy model
interactionFindings.detail: Architecture/07 requires convergence-exhausted and required-coverage-missing to share exit class 3 while carrying distinct reason codes because their remedies differ. TO-7 calls that a defect. Exit classes are automation dispositions; reason codes are remedy-specific.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Replace TO-7 with separate class-level automation stability and reason-level remedy discrimination invariants.

interactionFindings.title: TO-11 and its falsifier collapse verdict back into termination
interactionFindings.detail: TO-4 makes verdict and termination orthogonal; architecture/02/07 allow pass verdict plus operational termination when a required postcondition fails. TO-11's 'no verdict of any kind' and pass/fail-rather-than-operational falsifier erase that distinction.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Fail closed by preventing authoritative sealing/success, not by erasing a separately computed verdict.

interactionFindings.title: EC-3 whole-Run identity contradicts EC-6 per-attempt identity
interactionFindings.detail: Two executions cannot produce an identical whole Run when ExecutionId must differ per attempt. The parity object must exclude attempt/lifecycle metadata and compare exact Coverage, EvidenceDigest, and evaluation outcomes.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Rewrite EC-3 and the matching architecture/08 wording around a semantic projection with explicit equality preconditions.

interactionFindings.title: TO-5/10 apply safety rules at the wrong scope
interactionFindings.detail: TO-5 omits authoritative/required qualifiers and combines Coverage, durability, and export; TO-10 is simultaneously too narrow (empty only) and too broad (all best-effort partial queries). Their falsifiers use an undefined green outcome.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Split the axes and define authoritative versus explicitly best-effort claims.

interactionFindings.title: TO-8/9 do not establish the public class contract
interactionFindings.detail: The six primary classes and precedence are unnamed; simultaneous diagnostics are mishandled; additive-only behavior is candidate, incomplete for old consumers, and has circular/stale ownership with VERSIONING.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Bind named class semantics and primary precedence in D9, then assign evolution through one non-circular versioning owner.

interactionFindings.title: EC-1/3/7/8 do not yet define a testable lifetime-neutral authority boundary
interactionFindings.detail: Surface form is substituted for semantic equivalence, whole-Run parity is impossible, closure analysis overclaims runtime absence, and the four-way boundary leaves effectful work and publication unallocated.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Define semantic parity and a complete responsibility/authority table before deriving conformance tests.

interactionFindings.title: The invariant set remains incomplete even after incorrect rows are rewritten
interactionFindings.detail: D9 still needs envelope/process parity, pre-admission FailureResult, policy-not-Error/operational-not-Finding, orphan recovery, exit0-not-attestation, tombstone-backed expiry, and baseline no-comparison/no-derived-findings. R-1 needs cancellation, cleanup, progress/telemetry, effectful-provider placement, and publication ownership.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Add or explicitly rehome each property with a dependency and falsifier; absence cannot be repaired by broad totality language.

interactionFindings.title: v3 was rebound before the requested invariant review and still carries the unchanged rejected set
interactionFindings.detail: scope-correction v3 says TO/EC are unchanged and unreviewed, yet the register binds D9 and R-1 to the whole v3 artifact. Architecture/07/08 still say there is no accepted binding. The same premature-rebind error has now occurred on v1, v2, and v3 while check-claims remains green.
interactionFindings.requiredChange: Keep D9/R-1 bindingArtifact null. Record v3 as an incomplete candidate and rebind only after a revised invariant set passes independent proposition, interaction, falsifier, and handoff review.

resolves.B-TOEC-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: TO-7 must be replaced; it contradicts architecture/07.
resolves.B-TOEC-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: TO-11 must preserve verdict/termination orthogonality.
resolves.B-TOEC-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: EC-3 parity object must exclude ExecutionId and lifecycle metadata.
resolves.B-TOEC-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: TO-5/10 require authoritative/best-effort scoping and separation.
resolves.B-TOEC-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: public class semantics, precedence, and versioning ownership remain incomplete.
resolves.B-TOEC-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: lifetime-neutral authority/responsibility boundary is not testable yet.
resolves.B-TOEC-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: required D9/R-1 architectural properties remain absent.
resolves.B-TOEC-08: PRESENTATION-FIX-REQUIRED: v3 must not bind D9/R-1 before a corrected invariant set is accepted.

sealedPropertiesCovered: ARCH.RUN-MULTIAXIS — lifecycle, Coverage, verdict, and durability are orthogonal
ARCH.CONFINEMENT-HONESTY — process isolation is not a sandbox and signatures do not deny ambient authority
architecture/07 diagnostics — reason codes distinguish remedies within termination classes
architecture/03 concurrency — every evidence-writing host uses a multi-process-safe storage protocol
architecture/02 identity — ExecutionId is allocated per attempt while evidence identity is content-derived
knownLimitations: This review judges the current invariant text; it does not author the revised v4 invariant artifact or its executable handoff suite.
It does not adjudicate the unstable historical finding denominator in scope-correction v3; that is independently blocked by B-SCV2-01/02.
The exact long-term exit-class evolution policy remains product/versioning work, so TO-8 is classified unsettled rather than rejected categorically.

No shipping implementation source was inspected because the assignment is greenfield invariant correctness; load-bearing consistency claims were verified against the architecture and source artifacts that define them.
confidence: high on the TO-7, TO-11, EC-3/6, EC-1, and authority-boundary contradictions; medium-high on final TO-8 evolution policy
sealRecommendation: Do not bind or seal D9 or R-1 on TO-1..11/EC-1..8 as written. Preserve the sound ownership principles, replace the four incorrect propositions, split/scoped composites, correct falsifiers, add the missing invariants, and require a mandatory design handoff.
